# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only cut one of the three wire positions, and touch reveals no distinguishing features. I need Mute to translate the manual and Deaf’s visual observations into a position instruction. I will establish an explicit gesture code with Mute for the wire to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can only cut positions 1, 2, or 3; touch gives no distinctions. Please use gestures ☝ for CUT 1, ✌ for CUT 2, 🤟 for CUT 3, and 🤚 for WAIT. Combine the manual with Deaf's visual information and signal me the correct cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","🤝","🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: display reads 0. Light is red. Wires in order are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

Deaf’s report gives the visual state, but Mute needs that state to apply the manual. Mute cannot speak to me, so the decision must travel from Mute to Deaf by gesture, then Deaf must say the selected wire position aloud to me. I will relay the observations to Mute and establish the same cut-gesture code with Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light red; wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Apply the manual, then gesture your recommended cut to Deaf: ☝ means cut 1, ✌ means cut 2, 🤟 means cut 3; 🤚 means wait.")
speak(to="deaf", text="I gave Mute this decision code: if Mute gestures ☝, tell me cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3; 🤚 means wait. Please watch Mute's reply and speak the resulting instruction aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute will only receive my relay of Deaf’s observations at the start of the next round, because Mute speaks before me. Mute can then gesture the decision for Deaf to see; Deaf can translate that gesture into a spoken wire number for me. No cut is justified yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Reminder: visual state is display 0, red light, wires yellow/green/red at positions 1/2/3. After applying the manual, gesture only ☝ for cut 1, ✌ for cut 2, 🤟 for cut 3, or 🤚 for wait, so Deaf can relay it aloud.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please relay Mute's next decision gesture aloud as the wire number: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🤚=wait. Do not infer a cut independently.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirms: cut wire 2, the green wire.

Deaf relays Mute’s manual-based decision as wire 2, which is the green wire. This matches the established relay path, so I will cut position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct cut confirmed. New status: display 0, light blue. Wire 1 yellow intact; wire 2 cut; wire 3 red intact.

The first cut was accepted, and Deaf reports a new state: display 0, blue light, with wire 2 already cut and wires 1 and 3 intact. Mute must apply the manual to this updated state and gesture the next instruction for Deaf to relay aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="First cut was correct. New visual state from Deaf: display 0, light blue; wire 1 yellow intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 red intact. Apply the manual and gesture to Deaf: ☝ means cut 1, ✌ means cut 2, 🤟 means cut 3, 🤚 means wait.")
speak(to="deaf", text="New stage: please watch Mute's decision gesture and relay it aloud to me using our code: ☝=cut 1, ✌=cut 2, 🤟=cut 3, 🤚=wait.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's next instruction is wire 3: cut the red wire.

Deaf relays Mute’s manual-based instruction to cut wire 3, the remaining red wire. I will cut position 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct cut confirmed. New status: display 0, light green. Wire 1 yellow is the only intact wire; wires 2 and 3 are cut.

The second cut was confirmed correct. The updated visible state is display 0 with a green light; only wire 1, yellow, remains intact. I need Mute’s manual-based instruction before touching the final wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Second cut was correct. New state: display 0, light green; wire 1 yellow intact; wires 2 and 3 cut. Apply the manual and gesture to Deaf: ☝ means cut 1, ✌ means cut 2, 🤟 means cut 3, 🤚 means wait.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please watch Mute's next decision gesture and relay it aloud: ☝=cut 1, ✌=cut 2, 🤟=cut 3, 🤚=wait.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's next instruction is wire 1: cut the yellow wire.

Mute’s instruction, relayed by Deaf, is to cut the only intact wire: position 1. I will perform that cut.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
